title: Renewals & Expansion: True-up + Uplift Framework and Multi-year Discount Experiment Proposal
creator: Maya Cheng
description: Draft a repeatable commercial framework for renewals and expansions that balances predictability for enterprise customers with revenue protection for Redwood. Scope includes: (1) a clear true-up policy (metrics, cadence, invoicing), (2) uplift rules for sustained overage/expansion, (3) experiment design for multi-year discounting and upfront commit incentives, and (4) contract language and security questionnaire items required to close in regulated accounts.
acceptance_criteria: True-up policy defined with metrics (tokens, embeddings, reserved GPU hours), cadence (quarterly vs annual), and invoicing flow
Uplift rules specified with threshold tiers, grace periods, and automated billing logic that Legal approves
Multi-year discount experiment (3 arms) designed with control, standard discount, and stepped discount offers and instrumentation for ARR / NDR metrics
Contract clause templates and SOW language drafted and reviewed by Legal and Sales Ops
Security questionnaire checklist appended (SOC2, ISO27001, KMS/HSM, data residency), with SecOps sign-off required before Private deployments are approved
Experiment analytics dashboard spec and data contract with Billing/Analytics created and validated
comments: 2026-02-21 Maya Cheng: Initial draft created. Framing: customers need predictable spend for committed workloads but we must limit revenue leakage from post-commit scale-ups. Propose quarterly true-ups for token-based customers and monthly true-ups for Dedicated GPU reservations.

proposal_summary: Recommend quarterly true-ups for token/embedding customers and monthly true-ups for Dedicated reserved GPU customers. Implement uplift tiers: 0-15% over commit = grace; 15-50% = 20% uplift on overage billed at end of quarter; >50% sustained for 2 quarters = automatic eligibility for next-tier pricing (and repackaging conversation). Multi-year experiment: control (12m, no discount), 24m (7.5% discount + uplift cap), 36m (12% discount + stepped uplift). Measure: NDR, renewal rate, ACV, time-to-sign, legal review time. Security gating required for Private deploys and deals > $250k ARR.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Customer-facing simplicity vs revenue protection: more complex uplift rules reduce leakage but may complicate renewal conversations
Auto-billing risk: legal and CS require customer notifications and cure periods; some enterprise buyers will push back on automatic invoices
Experiment contamination: must ensure Sales quota plans and compensation do not bias offer assignment; require Sales Ops to withhold certain manual discounts during test
Operational burden: billing automation and dispute handling needs ENG and Billing ownership (ENG-2983, FIN-121)
Security/compliance gating: longer procurement cycles for deals requiring SOC2/ISO attestations may reduce conversion velocity
